topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture on the causes of cancer and sets out the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Concepts of Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Environmental Risks, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the core nature of cancer as a genetic and evolutionary disease driven by a combination of endogenous processes, inherited predispositions, and environmental exposures highlighted through epidemiology.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections contribute to malignancy, focusing on Burkitt lymphoma and Epstein-Barr virus.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how specific dietary, environmental, and chemical agents—such as aflatoxin, UV light, benzo[a]pyrene, and aromatic amines—undergo metabolism and induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: They analyze non-mutagenic drivers of cancer, including tumor promotion, inflammation induced by agents like asbestos, and the influence of host developmental stages on carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the experimental and analytical approaches used to prove carcinogenicity, ranging from mutational signature profiling and biobank epidemiology to in vivo and in vitro toxicological assays.
